title: JSON and CSV: structures and tables
subtitle: JSON stores structures; CSV stores tables. After parsing, check both types and meaning.
concept: JSON stores structures; CSV stores tables. After parsing, check both types and meaning.
intuition: Store a dictionary in a text file or organize a bill into table rows.
objectives: Numeric CSV fields arrive as text

body.title: Store a dictionary as JSON
body.text: json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False) converts a dictionary to JSON text. Remember the s in dumps as string. ensure_ascii=False leaves non-ASCII characters readable. json.loads(text) converts the text back to data. This uses a standard data format rather than merely saving a dictionary's printed appearance.

body.title: Read a small CSV table
body.text: Each CSV row is a record, and the first row can name the columns. csv.DictReader reads each row as a dictionary using those names. Here io.StringIO wraps sample text as a file-like object; io provides input/output tools. You can also pass a real file opened with open to DictReader. A small text table separates table handling from path issues.

body.title: Numeric CSV fields arrive as text
body.text: An amount field may look like 125, but row["amount"] is the string "125". Convert it with int to integer cents before adding. A complete project also checks column names, missing values, and negative amounts. Successful parsing does not validate each row. Likewise, check that parsed JSON has the dictionary or list structure you need.

formalDefinition.text: JSON converts between structures and text; CSV reads column-based records. Validate structures and values after parsing.

workedExamples.title: Add two amounts
workedExamples.problem: The CSV amount column contains 125 and 200, in cents.
steps: DictReader reads two rows by column name.
Convert each amount string to an integer.

answer.code:
import csv
import io
text = "category,amount\nfood,125\ntransport,200\n"
total = 0
for row in csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(text)):
    total = total + int(row["amount"])
print(total)

commonMistakes.claim: CSV numeric fields automatically become numbers.
commonMistakes.correction: Fields are text by default. Convert them explicitly before calculation.

commonMistakes.claim: If a file parses, its data needs no further checks.
commonMistakes.correction: Check column names, value types, and permitted ranges too.

practice.problem: Convert [1, 2] to JSON and back, then print its length.
solution: The restored list has two items.

practice.problem: Read a CSV amount of 50 and add 10.

answer.code:
import csv
import io
text = "amount\n50\n"
for row in csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(text)):
    print(int(row["amount"]) + 10)

practice.problem: With only a CSV header and no data rows, what is the total?

answer.code:
import csv
import io
total = 0
for row in csv.DictReader(io.StringIO("amount\n")):
    total = total + int(row["amount"])
print(total)
